verdict.tagline: Brutal vertical ascents paired with surprisingly smooth performance.
for_you_if: you want games that run well on modest hardware
you like survival systems tied to your stamina
not_for_you_if: you need reliable connection stability for multiplayer
you expect standard pause features during group sessions
you want predictable map layouts without progression blocks

distortion_flags.sentence: Review sentiment improves progressively as playtime increases past initial connection hurdles.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Initial players encounter connection errors, difficult multiplayer joining, and punishing climbing mechanics lacking pauses or saves.

claims.claim: Reviewers report connection errors mentioning photon network and unexpected disconnects during offline runs.

citations.review_text:
Playing a offline game - after about 15 mins the game dropped with an error message "Disconnected from photon". Was on a good run and was unrecoverable.
Why would an offline run be interrupted for client disconnects? Makes no sense to call it "Offline".
It was fun to play but these types of errors are annoying.

Game wont launch. "Failed to connect to photon network". I've spent hours trying every solution on the internet and the official discord essentially told me they didn't care, staff was unwilling to help and unpleasant. 

Wouldn't recommend , It's a coinflip if you even get to play the game at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that joining friends can be buggy or difficult.

citations.review_text:
Really good game! Had a lot of fun playing it with my friend. Good gameplay, graphics and customisation. 

However, joining friends can be improved a little bit as it is very buggy, at least for me.

Great game I would say that when i tryed to play it kept saying that i had to stop the already running game but other than that great game should play money worth funny to see your friends fall hard to play by yourself at first i did not like it but after you know how to play it fun

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the climbing mechanics and world generation as punishing, with limited routes up walls and janky controls.

citations.review_text: It's Peak. Got carried to victory on my first run by my two PEAK veteran friends. The UI is incredible and the game mechanics all fit together very well, even if the controls for climbing are a bit janky. Would Peak again.

This is a nice concept for a game, but the reality is that the climbing mechanics are punishing, the world generation doesn't offer sufficient opportunities or routes to climb up and there's no back-out option for when you're halfway up a wall.

I tried a few islands. On only one did I find a clear way up, and only a third of the way up the mountain.

I was playing on my own, on the base level of difficulty. The experience may differ with others.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the absence of a save system, pause feature in multiplayer, or checkpoints that save between sessions.

citations.review_text: The lack of checkpoints that can be saved between sessions and difficulty in resurrecting team mates makes it frustrating to play as a part game.  Just not fun.
Because there is no pause in multiplayer or a save option at all, this game is not accessibility friendly.

claims.claim: Reviewers request the addition of public matchmaking or unlisted lobbies for non-friends to join.

citations.review_text: [h2] All I want is to make lobbies and have non-friends join them (like Amoung us
It's a very good game but I wish that there was public lobbies

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players adapt to stamina functioning as health while navigating sudden difficulty spikes in later biomes and accessible graphical settings.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the stamina bar also functions as health, decreasing as players acquire more effects until passing out.

citations.review_text:
I know a [i]friendslop[/i] when I see one. A game subgenre where the lack of strong core mechanics and gameplay loops are replaced with incentives to get a reaction out of you with the cheapest possible tricks on the basis of your friends, not the game. 

This, is [b]not a friendslop. [/b]

This game took a lot of beating at first by being the headliner for the friendslop subgenre at first but the consistent fanbase proved otherwise. First of all, the game is extremely well made and well thought out. Everything feels intentional and none of them is frustrating, the gameplay loop is interesting, challenging, and full of variety and surprises. The world gen is really the cornerstone for this variety in gameplay and with each biome comes different challenges you must face. Other than that, its extremely rewarding and keeps you determined through all those challenges to reach the top to see the tail of that campfire smoke.

Other than that, the gameplay mechanics like the stamina bar getting replaced with various debuffs is very interesting and fun. I think that part of the survival gimmick is what makes the game so interesting in the first place, and the way that survival mechanic is neatly bound to everything that happens in the world around you is really complemental because it makes you feel more connected and inside the biome.

Obviously its way more fun with friends, obviously its way more unforgettable with friends. But that doesn't make it a friendslop. Not every coop game is friendslop and this game is a good anectode for all lazy friendslop developers out there trying to make a quick buck out of your 5 second reactions with simple gimmicks.

Really cool game.  There're plentiful ways to interact with the environment; you can toss a bean on the floor and grow a stalk.  There are also a lot of cool glitches, hopefully the balanced ones remain untouched.  The tech-potential this game has adds to the re-playability.  There's movement tech aswell.

But the thing I find the most interesting is the combination of your effects, health and stamina: it all sits on the same bar.  Your stamina acts as health, as you gain more effects your stamina lessens.  Once you run out of stamina, you pass out.  I've never seen anything like this in a game, such creative prowess.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that later biomes feature a significant difficulty spike compared to earlier stages.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Sacrificing Chillness for Difficulty[/h1]
The casual tone that made me like PEAK initially has been largely abandoned with the DLC releases.

I love what PEAK is supposed to be, but the grab system's inconsistency regarding small gaps really kills it for me. Additionally, the devs have, through PEAK's life-cycle, made the game more difficult, which personally does not sit well with what from launch was advertised as a difficult-but-chill climbing game. I feel like the game always wants me to be on-edge in Roots, Mesa, and Alpine. [b]I liked PEAK back when it was a tense-but-fun romp with friends, and it no longer feels that way with the new biomes being so frequent.[/b]

Even that, if grabs consistently worked on ledges rather than having a small chance to force a slide down to death, I'd be fine with the difficult aspects! Yet grabs sometimes won't latch, or the ground someone else is standing on acts for you as a slippery territory. [b]To be fair, this is a fairly rare occurrence! This has also been in the game since launch![/b] This is not a major issue in of itself (you can usually spam Space to escape it) despite being potentially run-killing, if not for the fact that the new biomes largely exacerbate the frequency. Its so frequent that it always catches back up.

Its the combination of the difficulty-spike and the grab inconsistency that changed my tone on the game. [b]PEAK now makes me more mad at the game than happy enjoying the company of my friends.[/b] It used to not be the case, and I miss that.
Roots is too difficult after update. Goes from a 3/10 difficulty on shores to 9/10 on roots.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that controls are easy to get used to, and the game includes multiple graphical and FPS choices that make it playable on slower computers.

citations.review_text:
The first time I played PEAK, I immediately understood what kind of game it wanted to be: pure fun. No stress, no pressure, no competition, just climb the mountain, either solo or with friends, and enjoy the journey.

The mechanics are simple and easy to learn, so even new players can get the hang of it quickly. The daily changing map keeps every run fresh and gives you a new challenge every time you play.

The community also deserves 10/10. It's easy to find people to play with, and experienced players are always willing to help beginners. No toxicity, just people having fun together.

The game is just... PEAK!  1000/10.

Wonderful! I adore it, even though I am NOT the best at it! But anyhow:

- The controls are easy to get used to in my experience.
- The srt/ animation style is so cute!
- Bugle.
- It IS hard.
- Has multiple levels, difficulties.
- Has a LOT of graphic choices and FPS choices/ game quality. Very important sinse I can not afford a good computer. It makes it playable even for somebody that has a very slow computer.

I recomend this game if you have patience and like a little challange! And like bugles.

(TIP: if you get a coconut, and are at the top, roast it before you eat it/ continue! It gives more food that way.)

citations.review_text:
[h1] The developers have stated that the game will NOT receive anymore updates after 'The Final Ascent' [/h1]

[b] There will be no new biomes, no new items, no new cosmetics after this update [/b]

The game is essentially just left to rot now, and the devs have also stated this is a common thing they do with all their games. I would advise you not to support such company
great game, I see new trailer indicates last big update, but I hope dev reconsiders

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game runs well and performs adequately on lower-end PCs and laptops.

citations.review_text: This game is really fun! Especially if your playing with a group, because then it becomes a screaming match of begging your friends for help while you slide down the cliff and PERISH. It's really easy to learn how to play the game, and once you know the basics your good to go. The only downside is that with a lower end pc the graphics tend to glitch out.

Wonderful potato-PC tolerant friendslop with ample opportunity for trolling your close ones in cooperative play and with greedy & meditative solo walkthroughs. Diverse enough in its mechanics and map routes to offer a lot of replayability, but consistent enough to allow for strategizing in advance. Some procgen involved in map creation may cause minor bugs or weird clipping on certain seeds, but I haven't encountered anything particularly game-breaking if you play the game as intended. Requires a bit of trial and error to figure out what (albeit quite minimalistic) settings work best for you, but overall it's really easy to get into, especially if you have an experienced player showing you the ropes literally and figuratively. 8.6/10.
my fav game to play with friends. It can also even run surprisingly well on low end laptops or PCs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing connection problems with other players and note that voices are muted by default upon opening the game.

citations.review_text: Good game. Some problems connecting to other players and for some reason every time I open it up it has all voices muted and I always forget and panic for a second. Other than that it's great! Kind of hard but in a fun way.

Really good game to play with friends and that's it.
You need mods to play multiplayer with randoms and depending on your region , it might as well be an upside if you don't have nerves of steel.

The ascent difficulties don't feel like they were intended for multiplayer which is why I've barely seen ascent 3+ games.

By far the biggest problems are the two dogs*it biomes Alpines and Roots.
On Alpines in singleplayer ascent 5+ you get both the cold from the wind and the night. And that blizzard feels like it comes every 20 seconds and lasts 30 seconds

The Roots is no doubt the hardest biome when all the bulls*it is present there:
-Spiders that force you to always look up so you don't get snatched and yeeted off the mountain
-Lakes of poison on certain maps
-Gas clouds that turn you zombie, covering 30% of the map
-Zombies that will chase you all the way to the top unless you trick them to jump off the mountain
-Bombs that yeet you and mustard gas bombs scattered around the map
-Hordes of beetles that gang up on you to yeet you off the mountain
-Strong wind that will push you off the mountain and even throw you all the way to the Shore if you have any balloons tied to you.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that map generation can occasionally produce impossible layouts with no climbable path unless the player uses tools.

citations.review_text: amazing multiplayer game, the gameplay is quite chill on lower difficulty so u can have a chill talk with your gang while climbing, sure there is no matchmaking feature but u can just join their official discord or fan server to find ppl. there is also tons of mods for QoL stuff. one thing i hate, sometimes the map generation decided to say ♥♥♥♥ you and generate the impossible map with no way to climb without tools

I will probably have to edit this review a little after the final major update arrives on the 11th, but I severely doubt I'll change my mind on whether the game is worth it. It is 100% worth it in the current state. The only criticism I could possibly give is that they have to manually update the game to change the map cycle because they're still working on the long term solution for map generation. I'm a little sad that there is a final (major) update coming but the game already feels more complete than a lot of games in the friend-like genre (this ain't slop chief) and considering the unexpected success story behind it, the development of these updates must have been pretty insane. If you buy this right now, before the big finale update even arrives, you will have a good time. It's better with friends but I've played solo enough to tell you that it's still pretty good. Even with my poor person graphics settings the visuals and ambience give a really nice "nature walk in solitude" vibe at base difficulty.
